reason: Re-opened the packet for Isa 1 (Sitarama Sastri, 1905 printing). The evidence words are there, and ‘covered by his self … I alone am all this’, ‘bound to renounce’ and ‘Bhnnjithah means protect’ carry most of the reading. But the sentence has Śaṅkara read the covering as seeing ‘all that moves’ as the Self, while his gloss on ‘whatsoever moveth on the earth’ explicitly widens it: ‘All this universe, movable and immovable’. The paraphrase narrows his reading to the verse’s surface word, a drift from his own words. verse.js ok (Isa Upanishad 1, at [0]); entry-check ok on the shipped entry. Plain sense (opening verse; renunciation, work, closing prayer with the body burned to ashes at 17) is acceptable, school rule not triggered with one commentator, no comparison, tone fine.
better: The Isa opens its eighteen verses, which run from renunciation and work to a prayer at the hour of death; Śaṅkara, commentary on verse 1, reads the covering as seeing all things, moving and unmoving, as the Self, whence renunciation, and ‘enjoy’ as protect. (entry-check ok, 45 words)
